title: 125. Swim in Rising Water

examples.explanation: Both routes from (0,0) to (1,1) have a maximum elevation of 3, making 3 the minimum time needed.
Every path from (0,0) to (4,4) must cross a cell with elevation at least 16, and there exists a path whose highest elevation is 16.

hints: A path's required time is the maximum elevation on that path; minimize that maximum.
Use Dijkstra's algorithm where entering a neighbor changes the path cost to max(currentCost, neighborElevation).
An alternative is binary search on time and a flood-fill reachability check.
